title: Gait disturbances and motor learning in patients with Parkinson's disease after implantation of a deep brain stimulation in the subthalamic nucleus.
summary: Deep brain stimulation of the subthalamic nucleus (STN-DBS) is a globally established and effective treatment option for patients with Parkinson's syndrome who suffer from complications (mainly motor fluctuations) of dopaminergic drug therapy. In the application of STN-DBS, electrodes are implanted into a brain region, the nucleus subthalamicus, of the patient.   Patients with Parkinson's syndrome develop gait disturbances and an increased risk of falls during the course of the disease due to a variety of causes. The STN-DBS improves gait disturbance only in some patients, why this is the case is currently unclear. Furthermore, it is currently unclear whether STN-DBS implantation already results in changes in networks that play a role in motor learning. Through network analysis, we aim to better understand the role of STN-DBS on motor learning and gait dysfunction in patients with Parkinson's disease.
conditions: Primary Parkinson's syndrome with moderate to severe impairment

interventions.name: Patients with Parkinson's syndrome who are implanted with deep brain stimulation in the subthalamic nucleus for clinical reasons. These patients are examined before and 9-12 months after implantation.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Presence of Parkinson's syndrome (according to UK Parkinson's Disease Society Brain Bank Diagnostic Criteria), indication for deep brain stimulation based on clinical indication and patient intended/consented, planned THS implantation in STN. Montreal cognitive assessment>23, BDI<19.
Exclusion criteria:
Pregnancy, current desire to have children or breastfeeding (exclusion by medical history), inability to walk or severe walking disability with inability to stand and walk freely, presence of severe orthopedic, psychiatric or internal diseases, contraindication for deep brain stimulation, lack of capacity to consent. Planned THS implantation in globus pallidus internus/ ncl. ventralis intermedius, Montreal cognitive assessment<23, BDI>19.
